model.name: Localization / Language
model.purpose: Bind governed language, locale, translation and terminology context to a host object, and govern who may declare, validate, approve, supersede, disclose and retire that binding.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-031 is a host-scoped mixin. It attaches to an object, field or resource owned by another model and carries: (a) language/locale identity, i.e. the canonical BCP 47 language tag or Unicode locale identifier that labels the host, together with its source, default and permitted values; (b) translation and fallback bindings, i.e. which localized variant realizes which source unit, at what workflow state, under which ordered language priority list, matching scheme and defined no-match behaviour, plus terminology and glossary bindings for the host subject; and (c) governance, i.e. accountable owner and role rights, release authority, provenance and confidence of declared and inferred values, pinned registry/profile/standard revisions, validation and reconciliation outcomes, conflict disposition, declarative disclosure and redaction rules, and binding version, effective interval, supersession, deprecation, retention, hold and tombstone. The mixin never creates an independent lifecycle for a language, script, country, person, content item or translation project; its lifecycle verbs act on the binding as it sits on its host object unless a separately identified resource is explicitly referenced. It is format-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, XLIFF, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: Host-scoped binding of a BCP 47 language tag or Unicode locale identifier to an object, field or resource
Recorded original tag alongside its canonical form, well-formedness status and validity status against a pinned registry snapshot
Declared source locale, default locale, permitted-tag set and ordered fallback / language priority list for the host
Matching scheme selection (basic filtering, extended filtering, lookup) and the mandatory defined behaviour when no tag matches
Translation binding: which localized variant realizes which source unit, and its workflow state (initial, translated, reviewed, final or profile-defined equivalents)
Terminology and glossary binding for the host subject, including references to concept entries in an external termbase
Provenance and confidence of tags, translations, terminology and machine-inferred or machine-translated values
Registry, profile and standard revision pins under which the binding was created and must be re-validated
Accountable owner, language/locale expert and translator/reviewer role rights, and release authority over the binding
Binding version, effective interval, supersession, deprecation and correction by supersession
Validation outcomes, reconciliation of declared versus observed content language, and conflict disposition among tags, profiles and content claims
Declarative sensitivity, embargo, locale-filter and field/resource-level disclosure and redaction rules for localized values
Retention class, legal hold status, integrity evidence and tombstone declarations for binding records
Declared interoperability crosswalks to translation-interchange, markup, transport and terminology carriers, recorded as alignments
out_of_scope: Lifecycle, definition or retirement of a natural language, script or country as a real-world entity; these belong to the ISO 639-3, ISO 15924 and ISO 3166 registration authorities
Maintenance of the IANA Language Subtag Registry, its registration procedure or its Language Subtag Reviewer decisions
Maintenance, vetting or release of CLDR locale data and its Survey Tool voting process
Lifecycle of persons, organizations or teams named as owners, translators or reviewers; only stable references to them are carried
Lifecycle of the host content item, product, document or dataset that the binding annotates
Translation project management, vendor selection, scheduling, cost, throughput and TMS workflow orchestration
Machine-translation engine operation, model training and evaluation methodology

Runtime policy evaluation, access enforcement and the tamper-evident audit trail; the mixin declares rules and references audit records but does not own evaluation, execution, enforcement or audit-trail semantics
Physical execution of destruction, backup, archival transfer or storage media control
Text rendering, font selection, shaping, bidi algorithm execution, character encoding and normalization semantics
Number, date, currency and collation formatting algorithms supplied by locale-data implementations
Authentication, credential issuance and identity proofing of principals

boundary_notes.neighbor: IANA Language Subtag Registry and BCP 47 registration process
boundary_notes.distinction: This model pins a registry File-Date and cites subtag records including Deprecated and Preferred-Value fields. It never assigns, deprecates, re-describes or retires a subtag, and it does not run the registration or Language Subtag Reviewer process.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Unicode CLDR locale data and UTS #35 locale identifiers
boundary_notes.distinction: This model references Unicode locale identifiers, likely-subtags operations and parent-locale fallback chains as pinned inputs. Locale data content, draft status, vote weighting and release approval remain with the CLDR Technical Committee.

This model binds source/target locale, workflow state and provenance to a host object. The XLIFF document, its segmentation, inline markup and module payloads remain the interchange artifact owned by translation tooling; the mixin only carries a reference and a state mapping.

This model expresses which agent generated or revised a bound value using PROV starting-point terms. Graph-wide provenance storage, qualified-influence expansion and provenance inference belong to the provenance model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Adopting-Dimension access-control, policy-evaluation and audit model
boundary_notes.distinction: This model declares sensitivity classes, embargo moments, locale filters and redaction rules as data. Authorization evaluation, enforcement at runtime and the tamper-evident audit trail are external; a reference to an audit record grants no ownership of audit-trail semantics.

This model declares retention class, hold status, integrity evidence and tombstone content for its own binding records. Appraisal authority, disposition execution, destruction and transfer are performed by the records system under the adopting Dimension's schedule.

This model supplies a programmatically determinable language value for a page or passage. Evaluating whether a delivered page meets SC 3.1.1 or SC 3.1.2, and remediating markup, are the renderer's and accessibility model's responsibility.

This model binds a host subject to concept entries and term references. The concept-oriented termbase, its metamodel, dialect and data categories are maintained externally; the mixin carries references and binding-level status only.

sources.title: RFC 5646: Tags for Identifying Languages (BCP 47)
sources.relevance: Normative syntax and subtag types for language tags, well-formedness versus validity, canonical formatting, Deprecated and Preferred-Value semantics, Suppress-Script, and registry stability rules that bound this model's identity and validation surface.

sources.title: RFC 4647: Matching of Language Tags (BCP 47)
sources.relevance: Language priority lists, basic and extended filtering, lookup with progressive truncation, and the normative requirement that applications MUST define defaulting behaviour when no tag matches; grounds the fallback-authority and resolve function.

sources.title: IANA Language Subtag Registry
sources.relevance: Authoritative subtag record structure (Type, Subtag, Description, Added, Deprecated, Preferred-Value, Prefix, Suppress-Script, Macrolanguage, Scope) and the File-Date used as the registry revision pin.

sources.title: UTS #35: Unicode Locale Data Markup Language (LDML)
sources.relevance: Unicode locale identifier structure, -u- and -t- extensions, canonicalization rules, likely-subtags add/remove, locale inheritance with parent-locale overrides toward root, and the divergences from BCP 47 (no extlang or grandfathered tags).

sources.title: CLDR Development Process
sources.relevance: A worked governance precedent for locale data: vetter/manager/TC roles with explicit vote weights, draft status ladder (unconfirmed, provisional, contributed, approved), release phases, and the statement that final release approval rests with the CLDR Technical Committee.

sources.title: XLIFF Version 2.1 (OASIS Standard)
sources.relevance: srcLang/trgLang binding, the translate attribute, segment state values (initial, translated, reviewed, final) with subState, and the Translation Candidates, Glossary, Metadata, Change Tracking, Validation, Resource Data and Size Restriction modules used as workflow-state and export alignments.

sources.title: Internationalization Tag Set (ITS) Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Data categories that map directly onto this mixin: Language Information, Translate, Terminology, Domain, Locale Filter, Provenance, Localization Quality Issue and Rating, MT Confidence, Allowed Characters and Storage Size.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent and wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, wasRevisionOf, hadPrimarySource, startedAtTime/endedAtTime used to express binding provenance without inventing a local provenance vocabulary.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative date-time format requiring seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z, plus the -00:00 unknown-local-offset convention; governs every timestamp in this model.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.relevance: SC 3.1.1 Language of Page and SC 3.1.2 Language of Parts (both Level A) require the human language to be programmatically determinable, which is the accessibility obligation this binding partially discharges.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Content-Language describes the intended audience rather than the language of all text, and Accept-Language carries a weighted language priority list for proactive negotiation; both are interoperability targets and a documented reconciliation hazard.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Lifecycle requirement categories (Capture, Maintenance and Use, Disposal, Transfer, Metadata, Reporting) with Must Have / Should Have classification, and the program-level versus system-level split used for retention, disposition and tombstone rules.

sources.title: ISO 15924 Registration Authority
sources.relevance: Confirms that script-code assignment, change requests and the Notice of Changes are external registration-authority responsibilities, keeping script identity outside this model's lifecycle.

sources.title: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority
sources.relevance: Establishes SIL Global as the language coding agency receiving and registering change requests, so language-code creation, change and retirement are outside this mixin's boundary.

sources.title: Language Tag Extensions Registry
sources.relevance: Registers the 'u' (RFC 6067) and 't' (RFC 6497) singleton extensions with the Unicode Consortium as authority, which constrains which extension subtags a locale profile may legitimately permit.

sources.title: Language Tags and Locale Identifiers for the World Wide Web
sources.organization: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) Internationalization Working Group
sources.relevance: Guidance that specifications MUST reference BCP 47 as a whole, that well-formedness is the baseline requirement while validity is a stronger authoring recommendation, and that language tags and locale identifiers are distinct concepts. Working Draft status, so treated as guidance rather than a normative requirement.

sources.title: ISO 30042:2019 Management of terminology resources — TermBase eXchange (TBX)
sources.relevance: Concept-oriented terminological metamodel, data categories, DCA/DCT styles and the TBX dialect mechanism; anchors terminology binding as an external resource this mixin references. Only the ISO catalogue record was verified; the full text is paywalled and was not read.

bundles.name: Localization governance, authority and conformance
bundles.description: Who is accountable for a localization binding, who may declare its defaults and fallback, how the origin and pinned inputs of every bound value are recorded, and how the binding is validated, reconciled, disputed and mapped to external carriers.
bundles.rationale: Language and locale values are supplied by external registration authorities and locale-data committees whose own governance is explicit about roles, approval authority and stability. A binding that carries such values is only trustworthy if it names its own accountable owner, records which registry snapshot and profile it was judged against, and states how competing claims are disposed of.

layers.name: Stewardship, role rights and declaration authority
layers.description: Accountable ownership of the binding, the roles permitted to propose, vet, review, approve and release changes, and the authority to declare source, default and fallback locales under a regional or organizational profile.

findings.name: Accountable stewardship and decision rights over the binding
findings.description: Names the party accountable for the localization binding on its host object, the roles authorized at each decision point, how distributed locale expertise is weighted, and what happens when no qualified authority exists for a target locale. Roles are references to parties governed elsewhere; only the assignment is owned here.

questions.text: Which named party is accountable for this localization binding on the host object?
answer_data: Responsible-owner party reference
Accountability scope (host object, field set or resource)
Effective start timestamp of the accountability assignment
Delegation reference where accountability is delegated

questions.text: Which roles are authorized to propose, vet, review, approve and release a change to this binding?
answer_data: Role identifier per decision point
Permitted operation set for each role
Separation-of-duties constraint between reviewer and approver
Reference to the authority source that granted the role

questions.text: How is contributor standing weighted when locale expertise is distributed across several organizations?
answer_data: Contributor standing level
Weight or vote value assigned to the level
Aggregation rule where one organization holds several contributors
Threshold at which a proposed value is treated as approved

questions.text: What is recorded when no qualified language expert or release authority is available for a target locale?
answer_data: Unstaffed-locale flag
Interim authority reference
Reduced draft status applied to affected values
Re-review trigger condition

data_elements.name: Responsible owner reference
data_elements.description: Stable reference to the party accountable for the binding; the party's own lifecycle is governed outside this model.

data_elements.name: Role assignment set
data_elements.description: Set of role-to-party assignments with the operations each role may perform on the binding.

data_elements.name: Release authority reference
data_elements.description: The body or role whose approval is required before a binding version becomes effective.

data_elements.name: Contributor standing level
data_elements.description: Declared standing of a contributor, used to weight competing proposed values for the same bound field.

artifacts.name: Localization stewardship charter
artifacts.description: Record declaring the accountable owner, role rights, standing weights, separation-of-duties constraints and release authority that apply to localization bindings within a governed scope.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative identifier issued by the adopting Dimension's governance register; where none exists, a governed IRI in the Dimension namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID assigned on creation.

findings.name: Authority to declare default locale, fallback chain and locale profile
findings.description: Establishes who may declare the host's source locale, default locale, permitted-tag set and ordered language priority list, which matching scheme governs resolution, and the mandatory behaviour when nothing matches. Profiles are declarative constraint sets; the resolution engine that consumes them is external.

questions.text: Who is authorized to declare the default locale and the ordered fallback chain for this host object?
answer_data: Declaring role reference
Approval evidence reference
Scope over which the declaration binds
Timestamp of the declaration

questions.text: Which matching scheme governs resolution, and what behaviour is defined when no tag matches?
answer_data: Matching scheme code (basic filtering, extended filtering or lookup)
Ordered language priority list with optional weights
Defined no-match behaviour (null result, designated default tag or error)
Whether parent-locale overrides supplement truncation-based fallback

questions.text: Which regional or organizational locale profile constrains the tags permitted on this binding?
answer_data: Profile identifier
Profile revision identifier
Profile scope (region, business unit, product line)
Precedence rank where several profiles apply

questions.text: Which subtag combinations does that profile require, prohibit or normalize away?
answer_data: Permitted primary language subtag set
Script subtag policy including suppression expectations
Region subtag policy for ISO 3166-1 versus UN M.49 values
Extension and private-use subtag policy
Variant subtag allow list

data_elements.name: Source locale tag
data_elements.description: The language tag of the authored source content that the binding's targets derive from.

data_elements.name: Default locale tag
data_elements.description: The tag returned when resolution over the priority list yields no match, or the declared no-match behaviour reference.

data_elements.name: Ordered language priority list
data_elements.description: Ordered, optionally weighted list of language ranges used for resolution against the bound targets.

data_elements.name: Matching scheme code
data_elements.description: Declared scheme governing resolution: basic filtering, extended filtering or lookup, optionally supplemented by parent-locale overrides.

data_elements.name: Defined no-match behaviour
data_elements.description: The behaviour applied after the priority list is exhausted; must be declared explicitly rather than left implementation-defined.

data_elements.name: Governing locale profile reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the regional or organizational profile whose permitted-tag and required-subtag constraints apply.

artifacts.name: Locale profile release
artifacts.description: Versioned declaration of the permitted tag set, required and prohibited subtags, extension policy, default locale, ordered priority list, matching scheme and no-match behaviour for a region or organization.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative profile identifier issued by the profile-owning body, qualified by an immutable revision identifier; where no master system exists, a governed IRI plus revision; otherwise a ULID per release.

layers.name: Provenance and revision pinning
layers.description: The origin, agent, method and confidence of each bound value, and the exact registry, profile and standard revisions under which the binding was created and must be re-evaluated.

findings.name: Provenance of tags, translations, terminology and inferred values
findings.description: Records how each bound value came to exist: human declaration, derivation from a registry record, machine detection or machine translation, together with the responsible agent, the activity, the prior version it revises and any confidence measure. Uses PROV starting-point terms rather than a local vocabulary.

questions.text: Which agent generated or revised each bound language tag, translation or term, and in what role?
answer_data: Agent reference typed as person, organization or software agent
Role played in the generating or revising activity
Activity start and end timestamps
Delegation chain where an agent acted on behalf of another

questions.text: What evidence supports an inferred or machine-generated value, and what confidence accompanies it?
answer_data: Generation method code (declared, registry-derived, detected, machine-translated)
Confidence or rating value with its declared scale
Detector or engine identifier and version
Sample or observation reference underpinning the inference

questions.text: Which prior binding version or upstream source is this value derived from or a revision of?
answer_data: Reference to the entity the value was derived from
Revision relationship to the preceding binding version
Primary-source reference where the value originates outside the system
Derivation kind (translation, transliteration, correction, import)

questions.text: At what confidence threshold must an inferred locale or translation be escalated to human review?
answer_data: Threshold value and scale
Escalation target role
Draft status applied below the threshold
Whether below-threshold values may be exported

data_elements.name: Provenance agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the person, organization or software agent attributed with generating or revising a bound value.

data_elements.name: Generation method code
data_elements.description: How the value was produced: human declaration, registry derivation, automatic detection or machine translation.

data_elements.name: Confidence value
data_elements.description: Machine-translation or detection confidence with an explicitly declared scale; never comparable across engines without that scale.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the entity or prior binding version from which this value was derived or revised.

data_elements.name: Provenance activity time
data_elements.description: Start and end times of the generating or revising activity, recorded separately from the moment the assertion was ingested.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance here is a set of assertions attached to individual bound values, not a document. The standards this model aligns with express provenance as inline annotations on the annotated node and as graph triples over agents, activities and entities, so materializing a separate provenance file would duplicate the binding record and create a second place where agent attribution could drift. Any durable provenance document, signed statement or evidence package is owned by the referenced provenance and records models, and is carried here only as a reference.

findings.name: Registry, profile and standard revision pins
findings.description: Captures the exact external revisions under which a binding was interpreted and judged valid, so that a later registry or profile advance produces a detectable re-validation obligation rather than a silent change in meaning.

questions.text: Which language subtag registry revision was in force when this binding was validated?
answer_data: Registry File-Date value
Validation timestamp
Whether validity was asserted or only well-formedness
Registry retrieval reference

questions.text: Which locale-data release and profile revision were pinned for fallback and likely-subtag resolution?
answer_data: Locale data release version
Profile revision identifier
Parent-locale override set applied
Likely-subtags operation applied (add, remove or none)

questions.text: Which exchange-format and terminology standard versions does this binding claim alignment with?
answer_data: Translation-interchange format version
Markup annotation standard version
Terminology exchange standard edition and dialect
Extension singleton registry revision

questions.text: What triggers re-validation when a pinned registry, profile or standard revision advances?
answer_data: Drift-detection trigger condition
Grace interval before the binding is marked stale
Role notified on drift
Automatic versus manual re-validation flag

data_elements.name: Subtag registry revision pin
data_elements.description: The registry File-Date under which the bound tag's validity was determined.

data_elements.name: Locale data release pin
data_elements.description: The locale-data release version used for canonicalization, likely subtags and parent-locale fallback.

data_elements.name: Aligned standard version set
data_elements.description: Versions of exchange, markup and terminology standards against which alignment is asserted.

data_elements.name: Pin staleness state
data_elements.description: Whether the pinned revisions are current, superseded but tolerated, or stale and requiring re-validation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Revision pins are scalar version identifiers and dates carried directly on the binding record; they are meaningful only in the context of the single binding they qualify. Emitting them as a standalone manifest would detach them from the value whose interpretation they fix and would invite a stale second copy. The pinned registries, locale-data releases and standard texts are themselves external artifacts owned by their publishers and are referenced, not reproduced.

layers.name: Validation, conflict disposition and interoperability
layers.description: Checks that determine whether a binding is well-formed, valid, canonical and profile-conformant; how contradictory localization claims are ranked and disposed; and how the binding is mapped onto external carriers as evidence-backed alignments.

findings.name: Validation, canonicalization and reconciliation of declared against observed language
findings.description: Defines the conformance checks applied to a binding and how a declared tag is reconciled against detected or transport-asserted content language, while preserving the originally recorded tag so that canonicalization and deprecation mapping never destroy the input.

Canonical form of the tag

Failed constraint identifiers
Severity of each failure
Waiver reference where a failure is accepted

questions.text: How is a deprecated subtag with a preferred value mapped without silently rewriting the recorded original?
answer_data: Recorded original tag as supplied
Mapped preferred value
Mapping rule reference and registry revision used
Whether the mapping is advisory or applied on write

questions.text: How is the declared tag reconciled against detected or transport-asserted content language?
answer_data: Detected language tag and detector confidence
Transport-level language claim value
Agreement or divergence result
Reconciliation outcome and the value treated as authoritative

data_elements.name: Validation status set

data_elements.name: Observed content language

Disposition decisions are localization decisions; enforcement of the outcome belongs to the consuming system.

Winning value and losing values

questions.text: How is a conflict between a macrolanguage tag and a more specific individual-language tag recorded?

Profile preference between the two
Whether both are retained or one is normalized away
Downstream matching impact note

questions.text: What is recorded when a cultural or accessibility review cannot be completed for a target locale?
answer_data: Review type that could not be completed
Reason code (no qualified reviewer, disputed conventions, insufficient corpus)

Re-review trigger and target date
