bundles.name: Binding lifecycle, disclosure and disposition
bundles.description: The governed lifecycle of the binding on its host object, and the declarative rules that control who may see localized values, how long binding records are kept, and what survives their withdrawal.
bundles.rationale: A localization binding changes far more often than the host it annotates and far more often than the registries it cites, so it needs its own version, effective interval and supersession semantics without acquiring an independent identity as a language, content item or project. Localized variants are also routinely embargoed or locale-restricted before release, and binding records fall under the adopting organization's retention schedule, so disclosure and disposition must be declared explicitly and their execution attributed to the owning systems.

layers.name: Binding state, version and supersession
layers.description: Workflow state and permitted transitions for the binding, its monotonic version and effective interval, and how superseded or deprecated versions are represented so that correction never rewrites history in place.

findings.name: Binding state, version, effective interval, supersession and deprecation
findings.description: Governs the lifecycle of the binding itself on its host object: current workflow state and permitted transitions, monotonic version, interval over which a version is authoritative, supersession by a successor, deprecation with replacement guidance, and correction performed by issuing a superseding version rather than mutating a published one.

questions.text: What is the current workflow state of this binding and which transitions are permitted from it?
answer_data: Current state code with the mapped interchange state
Optional sub-state refinement
Permitted next states and the role required for each
Whether the state permits export or publication

questions.text: Over which effective interval is this binding version authoritative for the host object?
answer_data: Effective-from timestamp
Effective-to timestamp or open-ended marker
Recording timestamp distinct from the effective-from value
Interval overlap policy with sibling bindings on the same host

questions.text: Which binding version supersedes or is superseded by this one, and on what ground?
answer_data: Predecessor binding version reference
Successor binding version reference
Supersession ground code (correction, retranslation, profile change, registry drift)
Monotonic version number or concurrency token

questions.text: How is an erroneous published binding corrected without destroying the superseded record?
answer_data: Correction event reference
Superseded version retained in place with a closed effective interval
Correction rationale text
Notification obligation to downstream consumers

questions.text: When is a binding deprecated with replacement guidance rather than withdrawn outright?
answer_data: Deprecation flag and deprecation timestamp
Preferred replacement binding or tag reference
Sunset date after which resolution must stop returning the value
Consumer migration guidance text

data_elements.name: Binding workflow state
data_elements.description: Current governed state of the binding, mapped to an interchange state value where one applies.

data_elements.name: Binding version token
data_elements.description: Monotonic version or concurrency token identifying this revision of the binding on its host.

data_elements.name: Effective interval
data_elements.description: Interval over which this binding version is authoritative, recorded separately from the moment the record was written.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the predecessor or successor binding version, with the supersession ground.

data_elements.name: Deprecation marker
data_elements.description: Flag, timestamp, preferred replacement and sunset date applied when a binding is deprecated rather than withdrawn.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This model is a mixin: the binding lives as a field set on a host object owned by another model, and its state, version, effective interval and supersession references are inline scalars and references on that same record. Materializing them as a standalone artifact would create a second identity for something that deliberately has none, and would risk being mistaken for an independent lifecycle for a language, content item or translation project. Where a durable narrative of change is required, it is carried by the host model's revision history and by the referenced records model, both of which are cited rather than reproduced here.

layers.name: Disclosure, redaction, retention and disposition
layers.description: Declarative sensitivity, embargo and locale-filter rules for localized values and their export redaction, and the retention class, legal hold status, integrity evidence and tombstone content that govern binding records at end of life.

findings.name: Sensitivity, embargo and field-level disclosure of localized content
findings.description: Classifies which localized fields or resources are restricted, embargoed until a release moment, or filtered to specific locales, and states the redaction or substitution applied on export. These are declarations consumed by an external authorization component; evaluation and enforcement are not owned here.

questions.text: Which localized fields or resources are restricted, and to which audience classes?
answer_data: Field or resource path within the binding
Sensitivity classification code
Permitted audience class identifiers
Locale filter expression limiting applicability to named locales

questions.text: Until what moment is a localized variant embargoed, and what may be disclosed before it?
answer_data: Embargo-until timestamp
Pre-embargo disclosable subset
Release authority permitted to lift the embargo early
Behaviour when the embargo moment passes without approval

questions.text: Does the localized value contain personal or otherwise regulated data that constrains disclosure?
answer_data: Regulated-data category flag
Jurisdiction whose rules were assessed
Basis reference for the constraint
Minimization or pseudonymization applied to the localized value

questions.text: What redaction or substitution is applied when an unauthorized audience requests the binding?
answer_data: Redaction strategy code (omit, mask, substitute fallback locale, deny)
Substituted value where applicable
Whether the redaction itself is signalled to the requester
Reference to the enforcing component

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Declared sensitivity class of a localized field or resource within the binding.

data_elements.name: Locale filter expression
data_elements.description: Expression declaring the locales for which a localized value is applicable or withheld.

data_elements.name: Embargo-until timestamp
data_elements.description: Moment before which the localized value must not be disclosed to the general audience class.

data_elements.name: Redaction rule
data_elements.description: Declared strategy applied to a restricted field on export or unauthorized read.

artifacts.name: Localized-content disclosure profile
artifacts.description: Versioned declaration mapping localized fields and resources to sensitivity classes, audience classes, locale filters, embargo moments and redaction strategies, for consumption by an external authorization component.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative profile identifier from the adopting Dimension's information-classification register, qualified by revision; otherwise a governed IRI plus revision, or a ULID per release.

findings.name: Integrity, retention, legal hold and tombstone declarations
findings.description: Declares the retention class and minimum period for binding records, whether a hold blocks disposition, what integrity evidence proves a superseded binding is unaltered, and what a tombstone must preserve. Appraisal authority and the physical execution of destruction or transfer sit with the records system.

questions.text: What retention class and minimum retention period apply to this binding record?
answer_data: Retention class identifier from the governing schedule
Minimum retention period expressed as a duration
Retention trigger event (creation, supersession, host disposal)
Owning schedule reference and its issuing authority

questions.text: Is the binding subject to a hold that blocks disposition, and who asserted it?
answer_data: Hold flag and hold identifier
Asserting authority reference
Hold start timestamp and expected review date
Scope of the hold across binding versions

questions.text: What integrity evidence shows that a superseded binding version is unaltered?
answer_data: Content digest value and algorithm identifier
Digest computation timestamp
Signing or sealing reference where applied
Verification result and verifier reference

questions.text: What must a tombstone preserve after a binding is withdrawn, and who executes the destruction?
answer_data: Retained identifiers and host object reference
Withdrawal reason code and withdrawal timestamp
Successor or replacement reference where one exists
Executing records system or policy reference for the physical destruction

data_elements.name: Retention class reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the retention class in the governing schedule that applies to the binding record.

data_elements.name: Hold status
data_elements.description: Whether a legal or administrative hold currently blocks disposition of the binding record, with the asserting authority.

data_elements.name: Integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the binding record content with its algorithm identifier and computation timestamp.

data_elements.name: Tombstone payload
data_elements.description: Minimal retained set after withdrawal: identifiers, host reference, withdrawal reason, timestamp and successor reference.

artifacts.name: Binding tombstone record
artifacts.description: Minimal durable record left after a localization binding is withdrawn, preserving identifiers, host reference, withdrawal reason and timestamp, successor reference, integrity digest and the reference to the records policy under which destruction was or will be executed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Retains the withdrawn binding's authoritative identifier so references do not dangle; where no master identifier existed, the governed IRI or the previously assigned UUID or ULID is preserved unchanged.

functions.name: Authorize binding operation
functions.description: Determines whether a requesting principal holds the role and authority declared for a requested operation on a localization binding, and returns a deterministic allow or deny with the governing rule reference. Identity proofing, credential issuance, enterprise policy-engine evaluation and the tamper-evident audit trail are performed by the adopting Dimension and are referenced, not implemented, here.
inputs: Principal reference and asserted role claims
Requested operation code
Target binding reference and host object reference
Applicable stewardship charter and disclosure profile references
outputs: Authorization decision (allow or deny)
Governing role or rule reference supporting the decision
Required additional approvals where the decision is conditional
preconditions: A stewardship charter or equivalent role assignment is resolvable for the binding scope
Separation-of-duties constraints between reviewer and approver are declared
effects: No change to binding content
Decision context is emitted for recording by the adopting Dimension's audit component

functions.name: Read binding
functions.description: Returns the localization binding for a host object at a requested version or effective instant, applying declared field-level disclosure rules to the response.
inputs: Host object reference
Optional binding version token or as-at timestamp
Requesting audience class
outputs: Binding record with recorded original tag, canonical form, state, version and effective interval
Applied-redaction indicator listing withheld fields
Pinned registry, locale-data and standard revisions
preconditions: Authorization decision is allow for the read operation
The requested version or effective instant resolves to exactly one binding version
effects: No state change
Withheld fields are omitted or masked per the disclosure profile

functions.name: Bind locale to host object
functions.description: Creates a localization binding on a host object with a recorded original tag, source and default locales, priority list, matching scheme and no-match behaviour, using a caller-supplied idempotency key so retries do not create duplicates.
inputs: Host object reference and target field or resource path
Recorded original tag and optional profile reference
Ordered language priority list, matching scheme and no-match behaviour
Idempotency key
outputs: Created binding reference and initial version token
Initial workflow state
Initial validation result
preconditions: The host object exists and accepts the mixin at the named path
Authorization decision is allow for the create operation
The supplied tag is at minimum well-formed
effects: A new binding version is created in an initial, unpublished state
Repeating the call with the same idempotency key returns the original binding without creating a second one
Registry, locale-data and profile revisions in force are pinned onto the binding

functions.name: Update binding
functions.description: Applies a partial change to an unpublished binding version under optimistic concurrency, rejecting the call when the supplied version token does not match the stored one.
inputs: Binding reference
Expected version token
Patch describing added, replaced or removed fields
outputs: New version token
Applied patch summary
Post-update validation result
preconditions: Authorization decision is allow for the update operation
The binding is in a state that permits in-place update
The supplied version token matches the stored token
effects: Binding content changes and the version token advances monotonically
A version-token mismatch fails the call with a conflict outcome and no partial write
An update attempted against a published version fails and directs the caller to supersession

functions.name: Unbind locale from host object
functions.description: Detaches a localization binding from its host object while preserving referential integrity for anything that cites the binding.
inputs: Binding reference
Expected version token
Unbind reason code
outputs: Unbind outcome
List of inbound references that block or survive the unbind
preconditions: Authorization decision is allow for the unbind operation
No hold blocks the change
Inbound references have been enumerated
effects: The binding no longer applies to the host object from the recorded moment
Where inbound references exist, the binding is closed rather than removed and a tombstone is prepared
Unbinding never deletes the host object or any separately identified translation resource

functions.name: Resolve locale for a request
functions.description: Resolves a requested language priority list against the bindings available on a host object using the declared matching scheme, returning exactly one result for lookup or zero or more for filtering, and applying the declared no-match behaviour when the list is exhausted.
inputs: Host object reference
Requested language priority list with optional weights
Declared matching scheme and no-match behaviour
Pinned locale-data release for parent-locale and likely-subtags handling
outputs: Selected binding reference and resolved tag, or the declared no-match result
Ordered candidate list with the match basis for each candidate
Indicator of whether truncation or a parent-locale override produced the match
preconditions: At least one binding exists on the host object or a no-match behaviour is declared
The matching scheme is declared explicitly rather than inferred
effects: No state change
The resolution basis is returned so that a downstream consumer can explain the selection

functions.name: Validate binding
functions.description: Runs well-formedness, validity, canonicality and profile-conformance checks against the pinned registry and profile revisions, and produces a dated validation report without mutating the recorded original tag.
inputs: Binding reference
Registry revision pin and locale-data release pin
Governing profile reference and revision
outputs: Validation report with per-check results and severities
Canonical form and any preferred-value mapping proposed
Overall pass, pass-with-findings or fail outcome
preconditions: Revision pins are resolvable
Authorization decision is allow for the validate operation
effects: A validation report is produced and linked to the binding version
The recorded original tag is never overwritten by canonicalization or preferred-value mapping
A fail outcome blocks transition to an approved state

functions.name: Reconcile competing language claims
functions.description: Compares the declared binding value with detected content language, transport-level claims and profile defaults, applies the declared precedence rule and emits a conflict disposition with rationale.
inputs: Declared binding value
Observed or detected language values with confidence
Transport-level content language claim
Profile default and precedence rule reference
outputs: Reconciliation outcome and the value treated as authoritative
Conflict disposition note with rationale and deciding role
Escalation flag where the precedence rule does not decide
preconditions: A precedence rule is declared for the scope
Confidence scales for detected values are declared
effects: A disposition is recorded against the binding version
Losing claims are retained rather than discarded so the decision remains reviewable
An undecidable conflict leaves the binding in a provisional state pending human decision

functions.name: Review binding
functions.description: Records a review outcome against a binding version, including declared limitations where a cultural or accessibility review could not be completed.
inputs: Binding reference and version token
Reviewer reference and review type
Review outcome and findings
Declared limitation where the review is partial
outputs: Review record reference
Updated workflow state
Carried-forward limitation statement
preconditions: Authorization decision is allow for the review operation and the reviewer is not the proposer
The binding is in a state that permits review
effects: The binding advances to a reviewed state or is returned for correction
Declared limitations are attached and survive later state transitions
Review does not by itself make the binding effective

functions.name: Approve and release binding version
functions.description: Applies the release authority's approval, sets the effective interval and moves the binding version to a published state; subsequent change proceeds by supersession only.
inputs: Binding reference and version token
Approving authority reference
Requested effective-from timestamp and optional effective-to timestamp
outputs: Published binding version with an effective interval
Approval record reference
Closed effective interval on the immediately preceding version
preconditions: Validation outcome is pass or pass-with-findings with accepted waivers
A review record exists where the profile requires one
The approver holds release authority and did not perform the review
effects: The binding version becomes authoritative over its effective interval
The prior version's effective interval is closed at the new version's effective-from moment
Published versions become immutable and can only be changed by supersession

functions.name: Supersede or deprecate binding version
functions.description: Issues a successor binding version that supersedes a published one, or marks a version deprecated with replacement guidance and a sunset date, preserving the superseded record intact.
inputs: Predecessor binding reference and version token
Supersession ground or deprecation reason
Successor content or preferred replacement reference
Sunset date where deprecating
outputs: Successor binding version reference
Bidirectional supersession links
Deprecation marker with replacement guidance
preconditions: The predecessor is in a published state
Authorization decision is allow and release authority is available
No hold blocks the change
effects: The predecessor is retained unaltered with a closed effective interval
Correction is recorded as a new version rather than an in-place edit
Deprecated versions remain resolvable until the sunset date, after which resolution must stop returning them

functions.name: Export binding with redaction
functions.description: Projects the binding into a requested external carrier using the declared crosswalk, applies the disclosure profile's redaction rules for the requesting audience, and states what the projection loses.
inputs: Binding reference and requested carrier with its version
Requesting audience class and purpose
Crosswalk revision and disclosure profile revision
outputs: Carrier projection of the binding
Redaction manifest naming withheld or masked fields
Lossiness statement for the projection
preconditions: Authorization decision is allow for the export operation
A crosswalk row exists for every element being projected
Embargo moments have passed or an early-release approval is present
effects: No change to the stored binding
Restricted fields are omitted, masked or substituted according to the declared strategy
The projection carries the pinned standard version so a recipient can interpret it correctly

functions.name: Dispose binding and write tombstone
functions.description: Evaluates retention class and hold status for a binding record, records the disposition decision and writes the tombstone, then hands physical destruction or transfer to the records system that owns execution.
inputs: Binding reference and all its versions
Retention class reference and elapsed retention trigger
Hold status and any asserting authority reference
Disposition decision and authorizing role
outputs: Disposition decision record
Tombstone record retaining identifiers, host reference, reason, timestamp and successor reference
Handoff reference to the executing records system
preconditions: The retention period has elapsed against the declared trigger
No hold is in force; an active hold fails the call without partial effect
Authorization decision is allow for the disposition operation
effects: Binding content becomes unavailable while the tombstone and integrity digest persist so references do not dangle
Physical destruction, media sanitization and archival transfer are executed by the referenced records system under the adopting Dimension's schedule, not by this model
A disposition attempted under an active hold fails with an explicit hold-blocked outcome

composition.target: Host object model designated by the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Attach language, locale, translation and terminology binding plus its governance to an existing object, field or resource without giving the binding an independent identity or lifecycle.

composition.target: IETF BCP 47 (RFC 5646 language tag syntax and RFC 4647 matching)
composition.purpose: Adopt the normative tag grammar, subtag types, well-formedness versus validity distinction, canonical formatting, and the filtering, lookup and mandatory no-match behaviour that govern resolution.
Carry a registry File-Date pin and cite subtag records including Deprecated and Preferred-Value, without assuming any part of the registry's assignment, deprecation or review process.

composition.target: IANA Language Tag Extensions Registry (u and t singletons)
composition.purpose: Constrain which extension singletons a locale profile may permit, and attribute their definition to the registered authority.

composition.target: Unicode CLDR locale identifiers and locale data (UTS #35)
composition.purpose: Bind canonicalization, likely-subtags handling and parent-locale fallback chains to a pinned locale-data release, while leaving locale data maintenance and its release approval with the CLDR Technical Committee.

Map source and target locale binding and workflow state onto the interchange format's attributes and modules for export, without owning the interchange document, its segmentation or its inline markup.

composition.target: W3C Internationalization Tag Set (ITS) 2.0 data categories
composition.purpose: Reuse Language Information, Translate, Terminology, Domain, Locale Filter, Provenance, Quality Issue and Rating, and MT Confidence rather than inventing local equivalents.
Express agent attribution, generation, derivation and revision of bound values in a standard vocabulary; graph-scale provenance storage and inference stay with the provenance model.
Reference concept entries and term records for the host subject and carry the correlation identifier and dialect pin, leaving termbase structure and maintenance external.
Attribute language and script code assignment, change and retirement to their registration authorities so no local code lifecycle is created.
Bind the resolve and export surfaces to proactive negotiation semantics and record the documented hazard that a content language header states intended audience rather than the language of all text.
Supply the programmatically determinable language value for a page or passage and record which conformance obligations remain with the rendering and accessibility layers.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension access-control, policy-evaluation and audit model
composition.purpose: Hand declared sensitivity classes, embargo moments, locale filters and redaction strategies to an external component for evaluation and enforcement, and reference its audit records without owning audit-trail semantics.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension records retention and disposition model
composition.purpose: Bind retention class, hold status and tombstone content to a governing schedule whose appraisal authority, disposition execution and transfer remain external.

composition.target: Regional or organizational locale profile registry
composition.purpose: Specialize the permitted-tag set, required and prohibited subtags, extension policy, default locale and fallback chain for a named region or organization, without duplicating the generic identity, authority or conflict machinery defined in this model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names a single accountable owner for localization bindings within its scope and a distinct release authority, and records both as resolvable party references rather than free text.

The Dimension publishes at least one locale profile revision that declares the permitted tag set, default locale, ordered language priority list, matching scheme and the mandatory no-match behaviour; a binding created without a resolvable profile is provisional.
The Dimension declares which registry, locale-data and standard revisions are pinned by default, and the drift-detection trigger that marks bindings stale when those revisions advance.
The Dimension binds its localization records to a retention class in its records schedule and names the records system that executes disposition, transfer and destruction.
The Dimension names the external authorization component that evaluates and enforces the declared disclosure and redaction rules, since this model only declares them.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers for bindings, profiles, crosswalks and reports are minted in a Dimension-controlled namespace and never reuse an external registry's identifier space. Language, script and region subtag values are carried verbatim from their registration authorities and are never minted, extended or re-cased into local variants; private-use subtags are permitted only where the governing profile explicitly allows them and are always accompanied by a human-readable meaning. Where a governed IRI is used, it resolves within the Dimension's namespace and remains stable across binding supersession.
registry_links: IANA Language Subtag Registry pinned by File-Date for subtag validity and preferred-value mapping
IANA Language Tag Extensions Registry for permitted extension singletons
Unicode CLDR release identifiers for canonicalization, likely subtags and parent-locale fallback
ISO 639-3 and ISO 15924 registration authority code tables for language and script code provenance
The adopting Dimension's own locale profile register, retention schedule and information-classification register

canonicalization_rules: The recorded original tag is stored exactly as supplied and is never overwritten; the canonical form and any preferred-value mapping are stored as separate, additional fields alongside it.

Canonical form follows the pinned tag-canonicalization rules: subtags lowercased except two-letter region subtags in uppercase and four-letter script subtags in title case, with duplicate variants and duplicate singletons rejected rather than silently deduplicated.

Where a Unicode locale identifier form is required, extension keywords and variants are ordered as the pinned locale-data release specifies and key-only true values are removed; extlang and irregular legacy tags are mapped to their preferred equivalents and the mapping is recorded.
A script subtag that the registry marks as suppressed for the primary language is retained if supplied but flagged as redundant; it is not deleted automatically.
All comparisons for equality are made on the canonical form; all display and audit reporting cites the recorded original.
patch_rules: Patches are expressed as explicit add, replace and remove operations against named paths and are rejected wholesale on any invalid path; there are no partial writes.
Every patch carries the expected version token; a mismatch fails with a conflict outcome and leaves the stored binding untouched.
A patch that would alter a published binding version is refused and the caller is directed to supersession, so correction always produces a new version and preserves the superseded record.
Patches that change the pinned registry, locale-data or profile revision force re-validation before the binding may re-enter an approved state.
Removing a provenance assertion, a declared review limitation or a conflict disposition is prohibited; such elements are closed or superseded, never erased.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field, an additional crosswalk row or a new non-blocking validation check is backward compatible and does not require a new profile major revision.

Narrowing a permitted-tag set, adding a required subtag, changing the matching scheme or changing the declared no-match behaviour is breaking and requires a new profile revision with an effective-from date and consumer migration guidance.
Deprecating a bound value requires a preferred replacement reference and a sunset date; resolution continues to return the deprecated value until the sunset date passes.
Alignment to an external standard is asserted only at a pinned version; advancing that version is a compatibility event that requires re-checking the crosswalk's lossiness statement.
Conformance to an external standard is never claimed without a named test or certification evidence reference; absent that, the claim strength is alignment only.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that owns the artifact, such as the governance register, profile register, information-classification register or records system of the adopting Dimension.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in the adopting Dimension's controlled namespace, where no authoritative master system exists.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension at creation time, used only when neither a master-system identifier nor a governed IRI is available.
A date, a language tag, a locale profile name or a version label is never an identifier; each may qualify an identifier but never substitute for one.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time strings that include seconds and an explicit numeric offset or the Z designator; a bare local time, a value without seconds, or a value without an offset is rejected. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they differ: the effective-from moment of a binding version, the provenance activity start and end times, the embargo-until moment and the withdrawal moment are event times, while the record-written, validation-run, detection and import moments are observation or ingestion times. Where the true local offset is unknown but the instant is known in UTC, the -00:00 offset convention is used rather than Z. Registry-supplied dates such as a subtag Deprecated date or a registry File-Date are carried verbatim as source-supplied dates and are never treated as event timestamps for this model's own lifecycle.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely the locale profile release, the binding validation report, the interoperability crosswalk and the disclosure profile, are named by a stable base identifier plus an immutable, monotonically increasing revision or run token that never encodes a date as the identifier. The base identifier is stable across all revisions; a new revision never reuses or renumbers a prior token, and a withdrawn revision keeps its token permanently reserved.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every published binding version and every serial artifact revision carries a content digest with a named algorithm and a computation timestamp, so that a superseded or tombstoned record can be shown to be unaltered. Digests are recomputed on read for verification but never overwritten in place; a verification failure marks the record as integrity-suspect and blocks export and approval until a named authority resolves it. Digest computation and storage are local; cryptographic signing, sealing and long-term evidence preservation are performed by the referenced records and provenance models.

policies: Least privilege applies to every binding operation: a principal receives only the operations its declared role permits, and the reviewer of a binding version may not also be its approver.

Correction is by supersession. A published binding version is immutable; errors are corrected by issuing a successor version with a supersession ground while the superseded record is retained with a closed effective interval.
No silent normalization. Canonicalization, preferred-value mapping and profile normalization always preserve the recorded original tag and record the transformation that was applied.
No unqualified conformance claims. External standards are treated as alignments pinned at a named version; conformance is asserted only where named test or certification evidence is referenced.

Declared limitations survive. A cultural or accessibility review that could not be completed, and a conflict that the precedence rule could not decide, are recorded and carried forward rather than resolved by silent default.

Declaration is not enforcement. Sensitivity, embargo, locale filter and redaction rules are declarations consumed by an external authorization component; this model neither evaluates nor enforces them and does not own the resulting audit trail.

read: Reads resolve a binding for a host object at an explicit version token or as-at instant; where neither is supplied, the version whose effective interval contains the current instant is returned.
Reads apply the declared field-level disclosure rules for the requesting audience class and return a manifest of withheld or masked fields rather than silently omitting them.
Reads return the recorded original tag, the canonical form and the pinned registry, locale-data and profile revisions together, so the caller can reproduce the interpretation.
Reads of a tombstoned binding return the tombstone payload with an explicit withdrawn indicator and the successor reference where one exists.
create: Creation attaches the mixin to an existing host object at a named field or resource path; a binding cannot be created without a resolvable host.
Creation requires a caller-supplied idempotency key; a repeated call with the same key returns the existing binding rather than creating a duplicate.
Creation pins the registry File-Date, locale-data release and profile revision in force at that moment onto the new binding.
Creation requires the supplied tag to be at minimum well-formed; validity against the pinned registry is asserted separately and may be deferred to validation.
A newly created binding enters an initial, unpublished state and is not authoritative until approved and released.
update: Updates require the expected version token and fail with a conflict outcome on mismatch, with no partial write.
Updates are permitted only on unpublished versions; an update against a published version is refused and the caller is directed to supersession.
Updates that change a pinned revision or the governing profile invalidate any prior approval and force re-validation and re-review.
Unbinding a locale from a host object closes the binding and preserves inbound references; it never removes the host object or any separately identified translation or terminology resource.
Approval and release are distinct from update: they set the effective interval, close the predecessor's interval and make the version immutable.
delete: This model performs no hard delete of a published binding record. Withdrawal produces a tombstone that retains the binding identifier, host object reference, withdrawal reason code, withdrawal timestamp, successor or replacement reference and the integrity digest, so that inbound references do not dangle.

Disposition is permitted only after the retention period declared for the binding's retention class has elapsed against its declared trigger, which may be creation, supersession or disposal of the host object.

An active legal or administrative hold blocks disposition absolutely: the disposition call fails with an explicit hold-blocked outcome and no partial effect, and the hold's asserting authority is recorded.

Superseded binding versions, provenance assertions, declared review limitations and conflict dispositions are never erased during the retention period; they are closed or superseded so the decision record remains reviewable.

Deletion execution is outside this model's boundary. This model records the disposition decision, the authorizing role and the tombstone; physical destruction, media sanitization, archival transfer and backup expiry are executed by the adopting Dimension's records retention and disposition model under its governing schedule, and by that Dimension's data-protection policy where a subject-rights erasure obligation applies to personal data inside a localized value.
A tombstone is itself a record subject to the same retention schedule; its own disposition is governed by the records model and is not initiated by this model.

roles.name: Localization binding owner
responsibilities: Holds accountability for the binding on its host object and keeps the stewardship charter current
Nominates language experts, translators, reviewers and approvers within the governed scope
Records the accountable delegation chain when accountability moves
Decides whether an unstaffed target locale is left provisional or removed from the profile

roles.name: Language and locale expert
responsibilities: Declares and justifies the tag, script, region and variant values for a locale within their competence
Advises on macrolanguage versus individual-language selection and on region subtag choice
Records declared limitations where locale conventions are disputed or insufficiently evidenced
Assesses whether a detected or machine-generated value meets the confidence threshold

roles.name: Translator
responsibilities: Produces target-locale values bound to a source unit and records the generation method used
Attaches terminology references for the host subject and flags terms lacking a concept entry
Advances a binding to a translated state without approving or releasing it
Records machine-translation engine identity, version and confidence where a value is post-edited

roles.name: Localization reviewer
responsibilities: Verifies a binding against the governing profile, the validation report and terminology bindings
Records review outcome, findings and any cultural or accessibility limitation that could not be closed
Returns a binding for correction rather than editing it when the proposer is better placed to fix it
Never approves a binding version they reviewed, preserving separation of duties

roles.name: Release authority
responsibilities: Approves a binding version and sets its effective-from and optional effective-to moments
Closes the predecessor version's effective interval at the successor's effective-from moment
Approves early lifting of an embargo and records the basis for doing so
Authorizes deprecation with a preferred replacement and a sunset date

roles.name: Localization records custodian
responsibilities: Binds the model's records to a retention class and monitors the disposition trigger
Records hold assertion and release with the asserting authority, and blocks disposition while a hold is in force
Prepares the tombstone payload and hands execution to the records system that owns destruction and transfer
Maintains integrity digests and escalates verification failures as integrity-suspect

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Every read, export and mutation of a localization binding requires an allow decision from the external authorization component against the roles declared in the stewardship charter and the field-level rules declared in the disclosure profile; absence of an applicable rule is treated as deny, not as permit.
exceptions: Locale-filtered content: a localized value marked as applicable only to named locales is withheld from requesters outside that filter even when the requester is otherwise authorized for the binding.
Embargoed variants: a localized value remains withheld until its embargo-until moment unless the release authority records an explicit early-release approval.

Regulated personal data inside a localized value: disclosure is further constrained by the adopting Dimension's data-protection policy for the assessed jurisdiction, which may override an otherwise permissive audience class.
Integrity-suspect records: a binding whose digest verification failed is readable only by the records custodian and the owner until a named authority resolves it, and is blocked from export.
Tombstoned bindings: the tombstone payload is readable by anyone authorized to read the former binding so references resolve, but the withdrawn content is not.
Break-glass access to an embargoed or restricted localized value is permitted only with a named authorizing role and a recorded justification, and triggers mandatory post-hoc review by the owner.
audit_requirements: Every authorization decision, export with redaction, approval, supersession, hold assertion and disposition emits a decision context containing the principal, operation, target binding version, governing rule reference and an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and an explicit offset.

Recording, storage, tamper-evidence and retention of these audit entries are performed by the adopting Dimension's audit component; this model emits and references audit entries but does not own the audit trail or its evaluation semantics.
Every redaction applied on read or export is signalled in a manifest so that a recipient can distinguish a withheld field from an absent one.
Break-glass access records the authorizing role, the justification and the post-hoc review outcome as a reviewable decision, retained under the binding's retention class.

required_fields: Pinned registry, locale-data and profile revisions
read_order: AGENTS.md, to establish the model name, type, and the specification, storage-type, interface and processes locations before any other read
The specification referenced by Specification URL, to obtain the boundary, in-scope and out-of-scope statements and the composition links
The governing locale profile revision, to obtain permitted tags, default locale, ordered priority list, matching scheme and no-match behaviour
The pinned registry, locale-data and standard revisions, so tags are interpreted under the same snapshot that validated them
The stewardship charter and disclosure profile, to establish role rights and field-level disclosure before reading or exporting any binding
The processes referenced by Processes URL, to select the correct operation sequence for bind, resolve, validate, review, approve, supersede, export or dispose
The interface referenced by Interface URL, last, because the storage format and access protocol are projections of the semantics established above

coverage.claim: This model gives a defensible, source-grounded governance, lifecycle and service structure for a host-scoped localization and language mixin: identity and canonicalization of the bound tag under pinned registry and locale-data revisions, declaration authority over defaults and fallback, provenance and confidence of declared and inferred values, validation and conflict disposition, binding version, effective interval and supersession, declarative disclosure and redaction, and retention, hold and tombstone with execution attributed to the records system. It does not claim complete or universal coverage of localization practice; project management, machine-translation methodology, rendering and formatting algorithms, and jurisdiction-specific erasure obligations are deliberately excluded and named as boundaries or gaps.

checklist.notes: Recorded original tag preserved alongside canonical form; identity priority puts the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed IRI, then UUID/ULID, and explicitly rejects a date, a language tag or a version label as an identifier. External correlation identifiers for interchange units and termbase concept entries are carried separately.

Workflow state with permitted transitions, monotonic version, effective interval, supersession, deprecation with sunset date and correction-by-supersession are governed on the binding only. No independent lifecycle is created for a language, script, country, person, content item or translation project; those are listed in out_of_scope and boundary_notes.

Mixin attachment to a host object, supersession links between binding versions, derived-from and revision links for provenance, macrolanguage-to-individual-language tension, and fifteen composition links each with source support and an explicit ownership statement.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z is mandated; event time (effective-from, provenance activity, embargo-until, withdrawal) is separated from observation or ingestion time (record-written, validation-run, detection, import). Registry-supplied dates such as a subtag Deprecated date are carried as source-supplied values and excluded from this model's event timeline.

Generation method, agent attribution in PROV starting-point terms, derivation and revision links, confidence with a declared scale, and pinned registry, locale-data, profile and standard revisions. Provenance is inline by design; durable provenance documents belong to the referenced provenance model.

Named responsible owner, six roles with distinct responsibilities, a release authority separate from the reviewer, contributor standing weights modelled on an existing locale-data governance precedent, and an explicit unstaffed-locale exception.

Well-formedness, validity against a pinned registry, canonicality, profile conformance, deprecated-subtag preferred-value mapping without destructive rewrite, and reconciliation of declared against detected and transport-asserted language, producing a dated validation report.

Deny-by-default with bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes; six exceptions including locale filter, embargo, regulated personal data, integrity-suspect records, tombstones and break-glass. Evaluation and enforcement are explicitly external, and the model emits but does not own audit entries.

Retention class and trigger, absolute hold block, integrity digest, tombstone payload preserving identifiers and successor reference, no hard delete of published bindings, and explicit attribution of destruction, sanitization, transfer and backup expiry to the adopting Dimension's records model and data-protection policy.

Versioned crosswalks to translation interchange, markup data categories, transport content negotiation and terminology exchange, each with a lossiness classification, a correlation identifier strategy and an explicit alignment-versus-conformance claim strength.

Matching scheme is declared explicitly (basic filtering, extended filtering or lookup), the ordered priority list is carried, and the mandatory defined behaviour when nothing matches is a required field rather than an implementation detail.
Terminology references for the host subject are bound with a correlation identifier and a pinned exchange-standard edition; the termbase structure and its maintenance are external.

The binding supplies a programmatically determinable language value for a page or passage, and explicitly records which conformance obligations remain with the rendering layer. Passage-level coverage depends on the host model exposing per-passage attachment points.

No primary source establishes a universal reviewer-qualification standard or an adequacy test for cultural review outside one consortium's vote-weight model. The model therefore records declared review limitations rather than asserting a review standard.

Regulated-data classification and jurisdiction assessment are carried as declarations, but no data-protection legislation was successfully retrieved as a primary source in this pass, so the specific erasure, restriction and storage-limitation obligations are attributed to the adopting Dimension's data-protection policy rather than modelled here.

The mixin carries confidence and quality-rating values as declared scales sourced from an external annotation standard, but defines no measurement units, instruments or calibration of its own; scoring methodology belongs to the quality and machine-translation models.

known_omissions: No records-management standard text was obtained as a primary source; ISO 15489-1 and the ISO 30042 full text were not retrievable, so retention semantics rest on a national archives authority's requirements plus the ISO 30042 catalogue record only.
No data-protection legislation was retrieved live in this pass; subject-rights erasure, restriction of processing and storage-limitation obligations are referenced by delegation rather than modelled.
Sign-language, oral-only and unwritten-locale governance is under-specified: script subtag policy and the notion of a canonical written form do not transfer cleanly to these cases.
Machine-translation confidence calibration has no cross-engine primary basis; the model requires a declared scale but cannot make scores comparable.

Bidirectional text, script-shaping and font-availability constraints that materially affect whether a localized value is usable are excluded as rendering concerns and are not represented even as a declared limitation field.

Pluralization rules, gender agreement and message-format placeholder semantics are locale-data implementation concerns and are not bound here, although they routinely break naive translation bindings.
conflicts: A tag may be valid under BCP 47 yet not be a canonical Unicode locale identifier: extlang subtags and irregular legacy tags are permitted by the tag standard but excluded from Unicode locale identifiers, and macrolanguage handling differs. The model resolves this by storing the recorded original and the canonical form separately and by pinning which canonicalization was applied.

Fallback is ambiguous across sources: truncation-based lookup and parent-locale overrides with likely-subtags produce different results for the same input. The model therefore requires the matching scheme to be declared explicitly rather than inferred.

A transport-level content language claim states the intended audience rather than the language of all text, so it is weak evidence of content language; treating it as authoritative conflicts with detection-based evidence. The precedence rule and conflict disposition make this choice explicit.
Registry Deprecated dates can predate the registry itself, so a Deprecated value is not usable as an event timestamp on this model's timeline; it is carried verbatim as a source-supplied date.

Well-formedness versus validity: specification guidance recommends requiring only well-formedness while advising authors to use valid tags. The model makes validity a profile-level constraint rather than a universal rule, which will disagree with adopters who expect validity to be mandatory.

Region subtags may be drawn from two-letter country codes or three-digit area codes with overlapping coverage and contested political meaning; no source resolves which to prefer, so profile declaration is required.
regional_assumptions: Region subtag choice between two-letter country codes and three-digit area codes is left to the governing profile; the model takes no position on contested territorial designations and treats such disputes as conflicts to be disposed of and recorded, not resolved.

Legal hold, records disposition and subject-rights erasure obligations vary by jurisdiction; execution is delegated to the adopting Dimension and the model only records the decision and the blocking condition.

Retention practice is anchored to one national archives authority's requirements, which is a defensible baseline but is not universally binding; other jurisdictions impose different minimum periods and transfer duties.

Cultural-review expectations, honorific and register conventions, and acceptability of machine translation for public-facing content differ materially by market; the model records limitations rather than asserting a common standard.
Accessibility obligations vary by jurisdiction and procurement regime; the model asserts only the programmatically determinable language value and leaves conformance evaluation external.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a normative requirement that a language tag must be valid rather than merely well-formed. The tag standard and W3C specification guidance require well-formedness of specifications and only recommend validity to authors, so validity was modelled as a profile-level constraint and flagged as a documented disagreement rather than presented as canonical.

Tested whether this model should own an audit trail, since it records approvals, dispositions and break-glass access. It should not: audit entries are emitted and referenced, while recording, tamper-evidence and retention of the trail are attributed to the adopting Dimension's audit component, and no function claims evaluation or enforcement semantics.

Tested whether a translation workflow state implies ownership of a translation project lifecycle. It does not: workflow state is a state of the binding on its host object mapped onto an interchange state value, and project management, vendor selection and scheduling are listed in out_of_scope.

Checked whether a locale profile deserves its own model rather than an artifact here. It was kept as a serial artifact plus an outgoing EXTEND link, so that a regional profile specializes permitted tags and defaults without duplicating the generic identity, authority, lifecycle or conflict machinery defined in this model.

Probed whether the model duplicates registry function by carrying subtag semantics. It does not: only a File-Date pin and citations to subtag records are carried, and subtag assignment, deprecation and retirement are attributed to the IANA registry and the ISO 639-3 and ISO 15924 registration authorities.

Attempted to justify a separate provenance artifact and rejected it: the aligned standards express provenance as inline annotations on the annotated node and as graph triples, so a separate document would create a second, driftable attribution record. The finding is inline-only with an external provenance model referenced.

Looked for a counterexample to correction-by-supersession, namely a case where in-place edit is required. Pre-publication drafts are the only case, and they are handled by allowing update on unpublished versions under optimistic concurrency while refusing it on published ones.

Checked whether declaring redaction rules amounts to owning enforcement. It does not: the disclosure profile is declarative data consumed by an external authorization component, and the export function applies rules without claiming to be the policy decision point.
